title: Startup Commands: CMD vs ENTRYPOINT ⚔️
description: Master the two most misunderstood instructions and learn when to use each.

slides.title: The Difference at a Glance 👀
slides.content:
# `CMD` and `ENTRYPOINT` Define Container Startup

Both specify what command to run when the container starts, but they interact differently with `docker run` arguments.

- **CMD** – provides **default arguments**; easily overridden by `docker run <image> command`.
- **ENTRYPOINT** – sets the **main executable**; `docker run` arguments are appended to it.

Think of ENTRYPOINT as the **fixed program**, and CMD as its **default parameters**.

slides.title: `CMD` – Default Command ⚙️
slides.content:
# Three Forms

**Shell form:**
```dockerfile
CMD echo "Hello"
```
→ runs `/bin/sh -c "echo Hello"`

**Exec form (recommended):**
```dockerfile
CMD ["echo", "Hello"]
```

**Default parameters for ENTRYPOINT:**
```dockerfile
ENTRYPOINT ["python"]
CMD ["app.py"]
```
If no arguments in `docker run`, it runs `python app.py`. If you pass `docker run myimage test.py`, it becomes `python test.py`.

> The last CMD in a Dockerfile wins. Only one CMD is effective.

quizData.question: If a Dockerfile has `CMD ["node", "server.js"]`, what happens when you run `docker run myimage bash`?
quizData.explanation: CMD is fully overridden by the command passed to `docker run`. So `bash` replaces `node server.js`.

slides.title: `ENTRYPOINT` – Fixed Executable 🔐
slides.content:
# The Immutable Entry

Exec form:
```dockerfile
ENTRYPOINT ["executable", "arg1"]
```

Shell form:
```dockerfile
ENTRYPOINT echo "Hello"
```

When you use ENTRYPOINT, the arguments from `docker run` are **appended** to the entrypoint command, not replacing it.

**Example:**
```dockerfile
ENTRYPOINT ["curl"]
```
`docker run myimage https://example.com` → executes `curl https://example.com`

> You can override ENTRYPOINT with `--entrypoint` flag in `docker run`.

slides.title: Combining ENTRYPOINT & CMD 🤝
slides.content:
A very common pattern: ENTRYPOINT is the tool, CMD gives default options.

```dockerfile
FROM alpine:3.18
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
ENTRYPOINT ["curl"]
CMD ["--help"]
```

Now:
- `docker run myimage` → runs `curl --help`
- `docker run myimage -v https://example.com` → runs `curl -v https://example.com`

The CMD arguments are appended to ENTRYPOINT. If you override CMD in `docker run`, it replaces the CMD part.

quizData.question:
Given:
```dockerfile
ENTRYPOINT ["ping"]
CMD ["-c", "3", "localhost"]
```
What does `docker run myimage google.com` execute?
quizData.explanation: The CMD arguments (`-c 3 localhost`) are overridden by the `docker run` argument `google.com`, but ENTRYPOINT remains `ping`. So it becomes `ping google.com`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## When to Use Which?
- Use **CMD** if you want users to easily override the command (e.g., `docker run -it ubuntu bash`).
- Use **ENTRYPOINT** when your image is a single‑purpose tool and you want arguments passed as parameters.
